episodes.title: Ruth E. Norman | This Cult Promised Aliens Would Build Us a College
episodes.description: In March 1976, a grandmother from El Cajon, California flew to London, walked into a Ladbrokes betting shop, and put down $4,000 that aliens would land on Earth within a year. She was that sure. Ruth E. Norman dressed like Glinda the Good Witch every single day, drove a Cadillac Coupe de Ville with a flying saucer bolted to the roof, and ran a group called the Unarius Academy of Science out of a San Diego strip mall next to a Little Caesars. Jaron and Tim trace how a fruit packer and milkmaid from Pasadena with an abusive childhood found spiritualism in the 1940s, married a palm reader named Ernest Norman the same day they met at a channeling conference, and got told she was the Pharaoh's daughter who protected Moses. After Ernest died in 1971, Ruth took over, renamed herself Archangel Uriel, and started channeling Tesla, JFK, Freud, Plato, and Oppenheimer. She bought 67 acres in Jamal with donor money so aliens could land and build a college. The 1976 Ladbrokes bet made her a televised curiosity. When the aliens missed the date, she blamed trauma from her past life as the goddess Isis and rescheduled for 2001. The episode also covers the followers who showed up to her hospital room in full costume to apologize for stabbing her in past lives, and how Heaven's Gate in 1997 flipped public opinion on alien cults overnight. Things I Learned Last Night is an educational comedy podcast where best friends Jaron Myers and Tim Stone talk about random topics and have fun all along the way. episodes.title: Urantia | Sleep-Talking Cult Leader: The Urantia Book & Celestial Seasonings Tea
episodes.description: Ever wonder about the story behind your favorite Sleepy Time tea? Discover the shocking connection between Celestial Seasonings and a 2,000-page book allegedly channeled from a sleeping man. In the early 1900s, a respected doctor made a discovery that would lead to a 2,000-page religious text—and eventually, a popular tea brand found in grocery stores across America. The story of Urantia and Celestial Seasonings blends religion, science, sleep talking, and spiritual mystery into one of the strangest faith movements of the 20th century. This is the story behind the Urantia Book, the movement it created, and how it connects to the tea you may already have in your kitchen.
